newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan denies Lee considering Australia visit.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan denies Lee considering Australia visit.

text.p: Taiwan President Lee Teng-hui would like to accept invitations to visit Australia but is not planning such a journey, contrary to a report in a Sydney newspaper, Lee's office said on Thursday.

Aides reached by telephone confirmed that Lee had met four Australian journalists on Monday for what he considered a private courtesy call during which they discussed the prospects for a private visit -- something sure to anger rival China.
Lee's aides denied a report in the Australian Financial Review quoting Lee as saying he was planning to make what the newspaper described as a "thank you trip" to Australia.
"President Lee has been invited previously to make speeches in Australia, but this is not a matter for just one side," one aide to Lee said.
"He said nothing about making a 'thank you trip' to Australia," the aide said from Lee's office.
The newspaper, which did not identify the source of its report, described Lee as wanting to thank Australia for its support during the China-Taiwan missile crisis in March.
It has been more than a year since Lee is known to have travelled overseas.

His high-profile June 1995 visit to Cornell University in the United States outraged Beijing, which downgraded its ties with Washington and punished Taiwan with a spate of military manoeuvres in waters near the island.
Since a civil war split them in 1949, Beijing has sought to unseat Taiwan's Nationalist government, which fled into exile on the island. China sees Taiwan as a rebel-held province.
The war games and missile tests peaked in the weeks before Taiwan's historic popular presidential election on March 23 in what Beijing acknowledged was a bid to erode support for Lee.
Lee and his vice-presidential running mate Lien Chan nonetheless won in a landslide, prompting some analysts to say China's campaign of military intimidation had backfired.
China refuses to have diplomatic ties with the 30 states that still recognise Taiwan's exiled Republic of China and assails even diplomatic friends who give quarter to Taiwan's leaders.
China formally protested Lien Chan's secretive visit to Ukraine in August and called off a high-level economic exchange with the former Soviet republic.
